FOREWORD 


This Indian Standard (First Revision) was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the draft finalized by 
the Pesticides Sectional Committee had been approved by the Food and Agriculture Divisional Council. 


Quinalphos aerial/aqueous flowable (AF) is used for the control of pests of agricultural crops. 


This standard was first published in 1996. In this revision, the standard has been brought out in the latest style and 
format ofthe Indian Standards, and references to Indian Standards wherever applicable have been updated. 


The composition of the committee responsible for the formulation of this standard is listed in Annex B. 


In the preparation of this standard, due consideration bas been given to the provisions of the 
Insecticides Act, 1968, and the rules framed thereunder. However, this standard is subject to the restrictions 
imposed under these, wherever applicable. 


For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, 
observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis shall be rounded off in accordance with 
IS 2: 2022. “Rules for rounding off numerical values (second revision)’. The number of significant places retained 
in the rounded off value should be the same as that ofthe specified value in this standard. 


IS 14410 : 2023 


Indian Standard 
QUINALPHOS AQUEOUS FLOWABLE — SPECIFICATION 
( First Revision ) 
1 SCOPE 3.2 Physical 


This standard prescribes the reguirements and the 
methods of sampling and test for guinalphos AF. 


2 REFERENCES 


The following standards contain provisions which, 
through reference in this text, constitute provision of 
this standard. At the time of publication, the listed 
editions were valid. All standards are subject to 
revision and parties to agreements based on this 
standard are encouraged to investigate the 
possibility of applying the most recent editions of 
the standards listed below: 


IS No. Title

:2019 Petroleum and its Products

Flash and Fire Points —

pesticide formulation 


3 REOUIREMENTS 
3.1 Constituents 


The material shall consist of guinalphos, technical 
conforming to IS 8072 dissolved in suitable 
solvent(s), together with emulsifying agent(s), water 
and suitable auxiliaries. 


The material shall comply with the physical 
reguirements specified in 3.2.1 to 3.2.4. 


3.2.1 Description 


The material shall be homogeneous and stable 
emulsion, free from sediment and/or extraneous 
matter. On dilution with water, it shall remain as an 
emulsion suitable for use as a spray. 


3.2.2 Cold Test 


When tested as prescribed in IS 6940, no turbidity 
or separation of solid or oily matter or both shall 
occur. 


3.2.3 Flash Point [Cleveland (Open) Cup] 


When tested by the method prescribed in IS 1448 
(Part 69), the flash point of the material shall be 
above 100 *C. 


3.2.4 Emulsion Stability 


When tested in accordance with IS 6940, any 
separation, including creaming at the top and 
sedimentation at the bottom, of 100 ml emulsion 
prepared in standard hard water with 2 ml of AF 
shall not exceed 2 ml. 


3.3 Chemical 


The material shall comply with the chemical 
requirements specified in 3.3.1 and 3.3.2. 


3.3.1 Quinalphos Content 


The nominal quinalphos content shall be declared 
[see 5.1 (f)]. When tested by the method prescribed 
in Annex A, the observed quinalphos content, 
percent by mass (m/m), shall not differ from the 
declared nominal value by more than the percent 
tolerance limits given below (see also 6): 


IS 14410 : 2023 


Nominal Value, Percentage 


Upto 9 


Above 9 and below 50 


50 and above 


3.3.2 Acidity 


When tested as prescribed in IS 6940, acidity (as 
H>SO,) shall not be more than 0.5 percent by mass. 


4 PACKING 


The material shall be packed in clean and dry HDPE, 
aluminium, properly lacquered mild steel containers 
or tinplate containers. It shall also conform to the 
general requirements given in IS 8190 (Part 2). 


5 MARKING 


5.1 The containers shall bear legibly and indelibly 
the following information: 


a) Name of the material; 

b) Name and address of the manufacturer; 

c) Date of manufacture; 

d) Date of expiry; 

e) Batch number; 

f) Net volume of contents, percent (m/m); 

g) Nominal quinalphos content, percent (m/m); 
and 

h) Cautionary notice as worded in the 
Insecticides Act, 1968, and rules framed 
thereunder; and 


Tolerance, Percentage 


+10 
-5 


+5 ofthe Nominal Value 


+5 
-3 


j) Any other information required under The 
Legal Metrology (Packaged Commodities) 
Rules, 2011. 


5.2 BIS Certification Marking 


The product(s) conforming to the requirements of 
this standard may be certified as per the conformity 
assessment schemes under the provisions of the 
Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 2016 and the Rules 
and Regulations framed thereunder, and the 
products may be marked with the Standard Mark 


6 SAMPLING 


When bulk manufactured material is offered for 
inspection, representative samples of the material 
shall be drawn as prescribed in IS 10627 and tested 
within 90 days of its manufacture. The criteria for 
conformity shall be as given in IS 10627. When the 
material is offered for inspection after 90 days of its 
manufacture, sampling shall be done as prescribed 
in IS 10627. However, the criteria for conformity of 
the material shall be the limits of tolerances, given 
under 3.3.1 of this standard. 


IS 14410 : 2023 


ANNEX A 
(Clause 3.3.1) 
DETERMINATION OF QUINALPHOS CONTENT 


A-1 GLC METHOD 
A-1.1 Principle 


The Quinalphos AF is dissolved in methanol along 
with internal standard and determined by Gas Liquid 
Chromatograph equipped with flame ionization 
detector (FID). 


A-1.2 Apparatus 
A-1.2.1 Gas Liquid Chromatograph 


A Gas chromatograph equipped with a FID detector 
is operated under the following suggested 
parameters. These parameters may be varied as per 
available facilities provided standardization is done: 


Column Glass, 2 m x 3 mm that 
1s, packed with 3 percent 
OV- 17 on 80 to 100 


mesh gas chrom Q 
Column oven 210°C 
temperature 
Injection port 250°C 
temperature 
Detector 250 °C 
temperature 


Gas flow rate Nitrogen, 30 ml/min 


A-1.2.2 Volumetric Flask — 50 ml, 25 ml. 
A-1.2.3 Beaker — 50 ml. 

A-1.2.4 Pipette — 5 ml. 

A-1.2.5 Micro Syringe — 10 ul capacity. 
A-1.3 Reagents 


A-1.3.1 Reference Standard Quinalphos — of 
known purity. 


A-1.3.2 Methanol 
A-1.3.3 Internal Standard — Di-n-butyl phthalate. 
A-1.4 Procedure 
A-1.4.1 Preparation of Internal Standard Solution 


Weigh 1.5 g of di-n-butyl phthalate in a 50 ml 
volumetric flask and make up the volume to the 


mark with methanol (see A-1.3.2). This will give a 
solution containing 70 mg/ml of internal standard. 


A-1.4.2 Preparation of Reference Standard Solution 


Weigh 0.2 g of quinalphos reference standard in a 
beaker. Add 5 ml of internal standard solution 
(see A-1.4.1). Shake well to dissolve and transfer 
careful to a 25 ml volumetric flask and make up the 
volume with Methanol. 


A-1.4.3 Preparation of Standard Solution 


Weigh sample containing equivalent to 0.2 g of 
quinalphos in a beaker Proceed as described in 
A-1.4.2. 


A-1.4.4 Estimation 


Inject 2.0 ul of the standard and. if necessary adjust 
the parameters and the column injected to give a 
complete separation within a reasonable time and 
peak heights half to three fourths full scale. Proceed 
with determination at least reinjecting each of 
standard and sample solutions in random order. 


A-1.4.5 Measure the peak heights of areas of 
quinalphos and internal standard solution. 
Determine the Ry values for each injected standard 
internal standard solution. 


A-1.4.6 Calculation 


Quinalphos content, percent by mass = 


— x xP 
RAT Ms 
where 
Bye Peak area of sample solution 
T Peak area of internal standard solution 
Peak area of reference standard solution 
R/T = 


Peak area of internal standard solution 


Ms = mass, in g, of sample taken for test; 


Mr = mass in g, of reference standard 
quinalphos; and 


P = percent purity of reference standard 
quinalphos.

BIS is a statutory institution established under the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 2016 to promote harmonious 
development of the activities of standardization, marking and quality certification of goods and attending to 
connected matters in the country. 


Copyright 


BIS has the copyright of all its publications. No part of these publications may be reproduced in any form without 
the prior permission in writing of BIS. This does not preclude the free use, in the course of implementing the

Review of Indian Standards 


Amendments are issued to standards as the need arises on the basis of comments. Standards are also reviewed 
periodically; a standard along with amendments is reaffirmed when such review indicates that no changes are 
needed; if the review indicates that changes are needed, it is taken up for revision. Users of Indian Standards 
should ascertain that they are in possession of the latest amendments or edition by referring to the website- 
www.bis.gov.in or www.standardsbis.
